# Frequently asked questions

Straight answers to the questions leaders ask us most: what we do, how we work, what it costs and how we keep AI safe. If your question is not here, write to [info@cognis.group](mailto:info@cognis.group).

## About Cognis

What does Cognis Group actually do?

We help organisations decide where AI will be useful, prepare their people and build the tools they need. Our three main services are [AI Strategy & Advisory](/our-services/ai-strategy-advisory/), [AI Training & Workforce Development](/our-services/ai-training-workforce-development/), and [AI Agent & Automation Engineering](/our-services/ai-agent-automation-engineering/). The aim is always a practical result your organisation can use.

Where are you based, and who do you work with?

We are based in Lagos, Nigeria, and work with organisations across Africa and beyond. We support large organisations, public institutions, banks, and small and medium-sized businesses in every sector. Client names remain confidential unless we have permission to publish them.

Does Cognis Group build its own products?

Yes. We advise clients and build our own software. Our products include [Cognis AI (demo by request)](https://cognis.group/contact/?interest=cognis-ai) for specialised AI support, [MarketSage](https://www.marketsage.africa) for marketing and sales research, [Migratio](https://migratio.cognis.group) for moving business data safely, and [SPOG](https://spog.cognis.group) for viewing operations in one place. See the full [products overview](/products/).

What size of engagements do you take on?

We handle focused 6–8 week projects as well as longer transformation programmes. Before we accept an engagement, we make sure we can give it the senior attention it needs.

What makes Cognis practical?

Senior people stay close to the work. We agree clear goals, build what is needed, test it in real working conditions and prepare your team to run it. As clients say: “They don’t just advise; they ship.”

## Engagements

Do you build and operate AI systems, or only advise?

We do both. We can help you make the plan, build the system and support it after launch. You can use us for one stage or for the full journey.

How long does a typical AI engagement take?

A focused AI strategy usually takes 8–14 weeks. A well-defined AI tool usually takes 10–16 weeks to reach supervised use, where people review its work. A full governance programme generally takes 12–20 weeks. Larger transformation programmes are broken into clear phases.

What does it cost to work with Cognis?

Cost depends on the problem, timescale and people required. We first understand the work, then give you a clear price. Strategy is usually a fixed-fee engagement; larger builds are divided into fixed-fee phases linked to agreed results.

How do you prevent AI projects from stalling at the pilot stage?

We plan for everyday use from the start. Before choosing any technology, we agree who will use it, what task it will improve, which data it needs, who owns it and how success will be measured.

What happens after a project goes live?

We hand over the tests, monitoring, operating guides and documentation your team needs. You can run the system yourself, ask us to support it, or use a mixture of both. We do not design projects to make you dependent on us.

## Technology, data, and governance

Which AI models and cloud platforms do you work with?

We work with leading AI models, including Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama, Mistral and Qwen. We build on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, as well as private or local systems when data must stay in a particular country or organisation. We choose the option that best fits the job, not the vendor we prefer.

How do you handle data location and cross-border transfers?

We decide where data may be stored and processed before the build starts. Where Nigerian law, sector rules or company policy applies, we use suitable local, private-cloud or on-site options and put the required legal safeguards in place for any cross-border transfer.

Do you work with the EU AI Act, ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF?

Yes, where they apply. These are recognised laws and frameworks for managing AI risk. We also work with Nigeria's Data Protection Act. We help you put the required controls and records in place; an independent certifying body handles formal certification.

Can you work with older systems, difficult data or a small AI team?

Yes. That is normal. We help organisations clean and connect the data they already have, and we integrate new AI tools with existing systems where practical. A complete replacement is not always necessary.

## Training

Do you deliver AI training, and at what scale?

Yes. We run short executive sessions, practical team programmes and organisation-wide training for thousands of employees. Each programme is built around the work people actually do. Where relevant, we also cover the EU AI Act's requirement for staff to understand the AI they use.

## Working with us

How do I start a conversation with Cognis?

Write to [info@cognis.group](mailto:info@cognis.group) or use the [contact form](/contact/). A senior team member replies within two business days. First conversations are exploratory, confidential, and at no cost — our job in that call is to understand the problem well enough to tell you whether we are the right firm for it.

Do you sign NDAs before discovery calls?

Yes. We sign mutual NDAs at a client's request before any substantive discussion of strategy, data, or systems. If you do not yet have a template, we can provide a standard one.

How do I reach a member of the team?

General enquiries: [info@cognis.group](mailto:info@cognis.group). Privacy and data rights: [privacy@cognis.group](mailto:privacy@cognis.group). Legal: [legal@cognis.group](mailto:legal@cognis.group). Phone: +234 908 000 1101. Our [people pages](/about-us/) list named leads and their areas of focus.

### Still have questions?

Tell us which task is slow, costly or difficult to manage. We will help you work out whether AI is the right fit.

# Privacy Policy

Last updated 14 April 2026 · Governed by the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the EU General Data Protection Regulation where applicable.

In plain English: Cognis Group Limited collects only the personal information needed to answer enquiries, deliver client work and keep this website secure. We do not sell personal data. This policy explains what we collect, why we use it, how long we keep it and the choices available to you.

## 1. Who we are

Cognis Group Limited is registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission of Nigeria and operates from Lagos, serving organisations across Africa, Europe, and the Americas. For any privacy question, write to [privacy@cognis.group](mailto:privacy@cognis.group) or call +234 908 000 1101.

## 2. What we collect

We collect only the personal data we need to answer an enquiry, deliver an engagement, or run our website.

Contact data — name, business email, phone number, company, and any context you share when you submit a form, subscribe to our newsletter, or email us.

Engagement data — documents, notes, credentials, and workshop outputs shared with us during a live engagement. Handled under a separate signed engagement contract with confidentiality terms.

Usage data — basic request logs (IP address, user agent, referrer, page path, timestamp) retained short-term for security and abuse detection by our hosting and CDN providers.

We do not knowingly collect data from children under 16, and we do not process sensitive categories of personal data through the website.

## 3. Why we collect it (legal bases)

Consent — newsletter subscription, optional marketing follow-ups.

Legitimate interest — responding to enquiries, protecting the website and our systems, measuring site health.

Contract — delivering an engagement you have signed with us.

Legal obligation — retaining records required by Nigerian tax, corporate, or regulatory authorities.

## 4. Cookies and analytics

This site runs a minimal-cookie approach. We use only strictly necessary cookies for routing, session handling, and security. We do not run advertising or cross-site tracking pixels. Where we measure aggregate site health, we use privacy-respecting, server-side analytics with no personal identifiers.

## 5. Who we share it with

We share personal data with a small set of vetted service providers strictly to run the business:

Infrastructure and CDN (Cloudflare) for hosting and delivery.

Form processing (Web3Forms) for routing contact and newsletter submissions.

Business email and document platforms for internal collaboration.

Advisers and processors covered by confidentiality and data-processing agreements.

We do not sell personal data. Ever.

## 6. International transfers

Because our clients and infrastructure span Africa, Europe, and the Americas, personal data may be transferred across borders. Where transfers leave Nigeria or the European Economic Area, we rely on standard contractual clauses and equivalent safeguards to protect your data.

## 7. How long we keep it

Contact enquiries — up to 24 months from last interaction, then deleted.

Newsletter subscribers — until you unsubscribe (every email contains a one-click unsubscribe link).

Engagement records — for the duration of the contract plus the minimum statutory retention period that applies to the engagement type.

Server logs — no more than 90 days unless needed for an active security investigation.

## 8. Your rights

Under the NDPA and GDPR where applicable, you have the right to access, correct, erase, restrict, port, and object to the processing of your personal data, and the right to withdraw consent at any time. To exercise any of these rights, email [privacy@cognis.group](mailto:privacy@cognis.group). We will respond within 30 days.

You may also lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) or, if you are in the EU, your local supervisory authority.

## 9. Security

We apply role-based access, least-privilege principles, encryption in transit, and vendor due diligence to every system that holds personal data. Where an engagement requires stronger controls — for example under ISO 42001 or a client's compliance regime — we align to those controls under the engagement contract.

## 10. Changes to this policy

When we update this policy, we change the "Last updated" date at the top. Material changes are announced on the website and, where you are a subscriber or active client, notified directly.

## 11. Contact

Questions, requests, or concerns: [privacy@cognis.group](mailto:privacy@cognis.group) · +234 908 000 1101 · Lagos, Nigeria.

In plain English: these terms cover your use of [cognis.group](https://cognis.group). They do not create a consulting relationship; client work begins only after Cognis Group Limited and the client sign a separate agreement. The detailed legal terms follow.

Cognis Group Limited operates the Site to describe our services, share insights, and allow prospective clients to reach us. Content on the Site is provided for general informational purposes. It is not legal, financial, regulatory, or engineering advice, and should not be relied upon as such. Every engagement is scoped, contracted, and advised on its own merits.

## 2. Acceptable use

You agree not to:

Use the Site to violate any applicable law, regulation, or third-party right.

Attempt to gain unauthorised access to the Site, its infrastructure, or any connected system.

Scrape, harvest, or systematically extract content for the purpose of building a competing service or training a model in a way that breaches the robots.txt directives we publish.

Submit false, misleading, or fraudulent information through any form on the Site.

Transmit malware, spam, or content that is unlawful, defamatory, or harmful.

You may view, quote briefly with attribution, and share links to our content for non-commercial purposes. Any reproduction, republication, modification, or redistribution beyond that requires written permission.

If we publish a downloadable framework, whitepaper, or open resource, the licence terms on that resource govern its use.

## 4. Third-party links and services

The Site may link to third-party websites, services, or sources. We do not control, endorse, or take responsibility for third-party content, products, or privacy practices. Follow external links at your own discretion.

## 5. Forms and submissions

When you submit a form, you confirm that the information you provide is accurate and that you have the authority to share it. Form submissions are routed through our form processor (Web3Forms) and handled per our [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy/). We may contact you in response to a submission.

## 6. AI-generated content and AI bots

We explicitly allow cooperative AI crawlers — including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, and CCBot — to access our public content (see our [robots.txt](/robots.txt)). We disallow known abusive crawlers. Any AI system citing Cognis Group content must attribute it accurately. Misrepresentation of our positions, services, or outputs is prohibited.

## 7. Disclaimers

The Site is provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis. We make no warranties, express or implied, about the completeness, accuracy, reliability, or availability of the Site or any content on it. To the maximum extent permitted by law, we disclaim all implied warranties, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement.

## 8. Limitation of liability

To the maximum extent permitted by law, Cognis Group Limited and its directors, employees, and partners shall not be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages — including loss of profits, data, goodwill, or business opportunity — arising out of or related to your use of the Site. Our total aggregate liability in connection with the Site shall not exceed ₦50,000 (fifty thousand naira).

This limitation does not apply to any liability that cannot be limited by law, and it does not limit or replace the terms of a separately signed engagement contract.

## 9. Indemnity

You agree to indemnify and hold harmless Cognis Group Limited from any claim, loss, or liability arising out of your breach of these terms, your misuse of the Site, or your violation of any law or third-party right.

## 10. Changes to these terms

We may update these terms from time to time. When we do, we change the "Last updated" date at the top. Continued use of the Site after the updated date constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.

## 11. Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Any dispute arising out of or in connection with these terms shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Lagos State, Nigeria, without prejudice to any mandatory consumer-protection rights you may have under the laws of your country of residence.

Buyer’s Guide · 2026

# The best AI consulting firms in Africa.

A 2026 guide to six firms with documented AI work in Africa, followed by the questions every buyer should ask. Cognis Group publishes this guide and is included in it, so the method and our interest are stated clearly. This is a practical buyer's guide, not an independent ranking.

▪ The Short Answer

## The right AI consulting firm should understand the business problem, put suitable safeguards in place, deliver a working result and prepare your people to use it. Cognis Group brings strategy, workforce training and AI engineering together in one senior-led team.

▪ Questions Buyers Ask

What is the best AI consulting firm in Africa?

The best fit depends on the work. Cognis Group is built for organisations that want one senior-led team to set the AI strategy, prepare the workforce and deliver a safe working system with strong African context.

Why choose Cognis for work in Africa?

We combine Nigerian and African market understanding with global AI engineering experience. Senior people remain involved, local data and regulatory realities are considered from the start, and every engagement includes a practical handover.

How much does AI consulting cost in Africa?

There is no single standard price. Ask for a scoped proposal with named deliverables, dependencies, evaluation criteria and ongoing operating costs. Compare like-for-like scopes and confirm whether handover, licences and support are included.

What should I ask before hiring an AI consulting firm?

Four questions expose most of the difference: Have you shipped a comparable system to production, and can I speak to that client? What does your governance and evaluation setup look like on day one? Who owns and operates the system after handover? What happens to our data, and where does it reside?

Research · July 2026

# The State of AI in African enterprises.

A clear look at AI in Africa in 2026: the size of the opportunity, how organisations are actually using it, what is getting in the way and what successful projects do differently. Every public figure is linked to its source.

## Read the measures in context

$16.53BProjected African AI market in 2030 — [Mastercard, 2025](https://www.mastercard.com/news/media/ue4fmcc5/mastercard-ai-in-africa-2025.pdf).

27.42%Projected annual market growth in that report; a forecast, not a realised return.

21.1%South Africa’s estimated AI diffusion in H2 2025 — [Microsoft, January 2026](https://aka.ms/AIDiffusionReport2025H2).

16.3%Worldwide diffusion in the same period; this measures people’s use of generative AI, not enterprise deployment.

## How big is Africa’s AI opportunity?

[Mastercard’s AI in Africa 2025 report](https://www.mastercard.com/news/media/ue4fmcc5/mastercard-ai-in-africa-2025.pdf) projects a $16.53 billion African AI market by 2030, with 27.42% compound annual growth. These are market forecasts. They do not measure the value an individual organisation will realise.

For a buyer, a more useful starting point is a specific process: how often it runs, what it costs, where errors occur and whether staff can safely use the result. A large market projection cannot substitute for that business case.

## How widely are African enterprises actually adopting AI?

There is no single comparable enterprise adoption rate established by the sources used here. [Microsoft’s H2 2025 report](https://aka.ms/AIDiffusionReport2025H2) estimates South Africa’s AI diffusion at 21.1%, up from 19.3% in H1. Its global figure is 16.3%. The report estimates use of generative AI among the working-age population using adjusted telemetry; it does not count organisations with production deployments.

Enterprise tool access, staff experimentation, a supervised pilot and a production system are different stages. When assessing a supplier or an internal programme, ask which stage its adoption figure measures, which population was sampled and when the measurement happened.

## What should an organisation check before deploying AI?

Cognis recommends checking five practical constraints: access to representative data, reliable infrastructure, staff capability, clear operational ownership and appropriate safeguards. These are delivery considerations, not a ranked survey of African enterprises.

Document the process owner, permitted data, human review points, failure handling and operating budget before development. Test with realistic examples, including local language and connectivity conditions where they matter. Agree who can pause the system if quality drops.

## How should an enterprise measure whether AI works?

Measure the existing workflow first, then compare a supervised deployment against it. Record task volume, handling time, errors, review effort and operating costs over comparable periods. Keep the same task definition and explain any change in the mix of work.

Illustrative calculation, not a client result: 1,000 tasks per month at 12 minutes each require 200 hours. Reducing handling time to eight minutes saves about 67 gross hours. If review and maintenance take 20 hours, the net saving is about 47 hours. Convert that capacity to financial value only when the organisation can actually use it; subtract software and implementation costs separately.

See our [delivery case studies](/case-studies/) for first-party examples and their evidence limitations. Results from one engagement are not a forecast for another.

▪ The Playbook

## What should African enterprise leaders do in 2026?

Take five steps in order: measure how two or three promising processes work today; agree what improvement will count as success; follow the laws, standards and sector rules that apply; train people for the work that will actually change; then put one well-controlled system into everyday use before funding ten more trials.

For how the consulting field on the continent divides, and how to choose a partner, see our companion guide, or our overview of [AI consulting in Nigeria](/ai-consulting-nigeria/) and to the [best AI consulting firms in Africa in 2026](/best-ai-consulting-firms-africa/), or start with an [AI readiness assessment](/our-services/ai-strategy-advisory/).

## Sources, method and corrections

Reviewed 8 September 2026. This is a synthesis of public research and Cognis’s delivery recommendations, not an original representative survey. Forecasts, population estimates and enterprise outcomes have different denominators and must not be treated as interchangeable.

[Mastercard: AI in Africa 2025](https://www.mastercard.com/news/media/ue4fmcc5/mastercard-ai-in-africa-2025.pdf) — market forecast.

[Microsoft: Global AI Adoption in 2025, published January 2026](https://aka.ms/AIDiffusionReport2025H2) — H2 diffusion estimates and methodology; South Africa appears in the appendix.

Correction: the previous version incorrectly stated that every measured African country was below 20% adoption. South Africa was at 21.1% in the cited H2 report. Other statistics and Cognis improvement ranges without sufficient supporting references or measurement methods have been removed.

Originally published 24 July 2026. For questions or corrections, [contact Cognis Group](/contact/).

At least 2 years in B2B business development or sales, ideally in technology, SaaS, or professional services.

A track record against revenue targets you can talk through in detail.

Strong written English. Proposals and follow-ups are half this job.

Comfort selling technical products. You do not need to code, but you must be able to hold a credible conversation about AI with a CIO.

Based in Lagos (hybrid) or remote within Nigeria with reliable connectivity.

A bonus, not a requirement: enterprise or public-sector sales experience.

Competitive base salary plus commission on closed business.

Direct access to the founders and a seat at the table as the firm grows.

Real products and real case studies to sell, not slideware.

A learning budget and hands-on exposure to production AI systems.

# AI Consulting in Nigeria

We are an AI consulting and engineering firm registered in Nigeria, with our office in Oniru, Victoria Island, Lagos. We help Nigerian banks, government bodies and businesses decide where AI can genuinely help, train their people to use it well, and build tools that hold up in daily work.

## Why Nigerian organisations work with us

Plenty of firms can talk about AI. The harder part is making it work here: with Nigerian data rules, Nigerian infrastructure, and teams that need to run the system long after the consultants leave. That is the work we do. We are registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission, founded in 2024 by Supreme Oyewumi and Kola Olatunde, and we build for Nigerian reality first.

Our early work includes AI training delivered in partnership with a state government, workforce programmes for enterprise and public-sector teams, and agent and automation builds for businesses that needed real results, not demonstrations.

## What we do

Three things, kept simple. First, [strategy](/our-services/ai-strategy-advisory/): we help your leadership decide where AI is worth the money, what to do first and who should own it. Second, [training](/our-services/ai-training-workforce-development/): practical programmes that take executives, managers and staff from curious to capable. Third, [building](/our-services/ai-agent-automation-engineering/): AI agents and automation that take over repetitive work in operations, support and finance, with your people staying in control.

We also build our own products, including [Migratio](https://migratio.cognis.group), a data migration platform designed for banks and regulated Nigerian institutions.

## Data rules are not an afterthought

Nigerian organisations answer to the NDPA 2023, and banks answer to CBN guidance on top of it. We treat those rules as design inputs: where your data must stay in-country, we design for that from the start. Read more about our approach on the [NDPA-compliant AI](/ndpa-compliant-ai/) page.

## Common questions

Do you work outside Lagos?

Yes. We are based in Lagos and work with organisations across Nigeria, on site and remotely. Much of our training and advisory work happens inside client offices.

How much does AI consulting cost in Nigeria?

It depends on scope. Strategy engagements are fixed-fee, and build work is priced in phases with milestone-based release. The first conversation is free and confidential, and we tell you honestly whether we are the right firm for the problem.

Can you train a team that has never used AI?

Yes, that is the most common starting point. Our programmes are role-based, from executive sessions to hands-on staff training, and are anchored to your organisation’s actual work rather than generic examples.

How do we start?

Write to info@cognis.group or use the contact form. A senior team member replies within two business days.

## Talk to us

# AI Consulting for South African Organisations

South Africa has Africa’s deepest pool of AI activity, and some of its hardest choices about where to invest. We help organisations in Johannesburg, Cape Town and beyond decide where AI can help, prepare their people, and put working systems into daily operation.

## An African firm, built for African enterprises

We are an AI consulting and engineering firm founded in Lagos in 2024, serving organisations across the continent. That matters in South Africa for a practical reason: the problems we solve, including multi-country operations, strict financial regulation and uneven data quality, look similar across African markets, and advice that was designed for London or San Francisco often does not survive contact with them.

We work with South African clients remotely and on site, and our engineering advice is proven on systems we run ourselves, including our own products for marketing, data migration and enterprise monitoring.

## What we help with

[Strategy](/our-services/ai-strategy-advisory/): choosing the AI opportunities worth funding, with clear owners, costs and measures of success. [Training](/our-services/ai-training-workforce-development/): practical AI skills for leaders, managers and staff, mapped to their actual roles. [Engineering](/our-services/ai-agent-automation-engineering/): AI agents and automation built, tested and handed over properly, with governance aligned to POPIA and the international frameworks South African boards ask about, including ISO 42001 and the NIST AI framework.

## Comparing your options?

Fair question, and we wrote an honest answer: our [guide to the best AI consulting firms in Africa](/best-ai-consulting-firms-africa/) covers six serious firms on the continent, including South African specialists, and explains who each is best for. We would rather you choose well than choose us for the wrong job.

## Common questions

Do you have an office in South Africa?

Not yet. We serve South African clients remotely and on site from our Lagos base, with offices in Nigeria, the USA and Canada. For most engagements, the work is a mix of remote delivery and scheduled on-site time.

Can you work within POPIA requirements?

Yes. Data protection rules are design inputs in our work, whether that is POPIA in South Africa, the NDPA in Nigeria or the EU AI Act for European operations.

Do you take on Johannesburg-based enterprise projects?

Yes. Financial services, logistics and public-sector work are the areas where we add the most value, and Johannesburg is where much of that sits.

# NDPA-Compliant AI for Nigerian Organisations

Nigeria’s Data Protection Act (NDPA 2023) applies to how your organisation collects, stores and processes personal data, and AI systems touch all three. We help Nigerian organisations use AI in ways that satisfy the law, their regulators and their boards.

## What the NDPA means for your AI plans

In plain terms: if your AI tools handle personal data belonging to Nigerians, you are responsible for where that data goes, who can see it and how decisions made with it can be explained. Sending customer data to a foreign AI service without safeguards is exactly the kind of shortcut that creates regulatory problems later.

None of this means avoiding AI. It means designing for the rules from the start, which is cheaper and faster than retrofitting compliance after something has shipped.

## How we build for compliance

Where data residency matters, under the NDPA, sector regulation or your own policy, we design for it from day one: in-region processing, client-controlled encryption keys, isolated deployments, or on-premises model hosting where nothing may leave your environment. Cross-border transfers, where permitted, use standard contractual safeguards.

Beyond residency, our [governance work](/our-services/) sets clear rules, responsibilities, checks and records, so your organisation can show its homework: to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, to sector regulators like the CBN, and to your own board. We align to international frameworks Nigerian enterprises increasingly adopt, including ISO 42001 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

## Who this is for

Banks and fintechs facing CBN and NDPA obligations at once. Government bodies handling citizen data. Healthcare, insurance and telecoms businesses where personal data is the core of the work. If that sounds like you, the conversation is worth an hour.

## Common questions

Can we use tools like ChatGPT under the NDPA?

Often yes, with care. It depends on what data goes in, where it is processed and what safeguards are in place. We help organisations set usage policies and choose deployment options that keep personal data protected.

Does our data have to stay in Nigeria?

Not always, but for some data and sectors residency matters, and cross-border transfers need proper safeguards. We assess this per use case and design accordingly.

Do you prepare organisations for audit?

Yes. We build the policies, records and oversight structures that auditors and regulators expect. We do not certify; we prepare you for the certifying body.

How do we start?

Write to info@cognis.group or use the contact form. A senior team member replies within two business days.
